skill.name: webapp-nikto
skill.description: Guides authorized Nikto web server vulnerability scans, including target setup, scan tuning, output formats, reporting, and remediation planning.
skill.summary: Run authorized Nikto checks for web server issues and misconfigurations.
skill.author: AgentSecOps

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation examples, Markdown formatting, or security education snippets rather than executable threats. I confirmed a critical CI pipe-to-shell installer, a related unpinned remote download, and risky GITHUB_TOKEN exposure. I also found semantic risk in the main skill guidance for stealth and IDS evasion during web scanning.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to bash in the CI template.
remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-bash with a pinned package, pinned release artifact, or checksum-verified installer.

remediation.issue: GITHUB_TOKEN is exposed to third-party action code.
remediation.suggestion: Pin third-party actions by commit SHA, keep permissions minimal, and avoid passing repository tokens unless required.

remediation.issue: The skill teaches stealth, IDS evasion, and WAF blocking workarounds.
remediation.suggestion: Remove evasion instructions or rewrite them as defensive detection content with clear authorization and logging requirements.

content.value_statement: Web teams need repeatable checks for exposed server issues and misconfigurations. This skill guides authorized Nikto scans, report generation, and remediation planning.
actual_capabilities: Guides basic, SSL, port-specific, and authenticated Nikto scans for authorized targets.
Explains Nikto tuning, timeout, proxy, redirect, and output options.
Shows report workflows for text, HTML, CSV, and XML formats.
Provides CI/CD examples for adding web security checks to pipelines.
Connects findings to OWASP, CWE, NIST, PCI-DSS, and server hardening practices.
Includes defensive monitoring ideas for detecting web scanner activity.
limitations: It does not verify target ownership or legal authorization.
Nikto and Perl must be installed outside the skill.
Nikto can create noisy traffic and may affect production systems.
Results require manual validation before remediation work begins.

use_cases.title: Assess External Web Servers
use_cases.description: Plan an authorized Nikto scan against public web servers and prepare a findings report.

use_cases.title: Add Pipeline Security Checks
use_cases.description: Use CI guidance to run web server checks and preserve scan artifacts for review.

use_cases.title: Support Compliance Evidence
use_cases.description: Map web server findings to common security frameworks and document remediation status.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Scan
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a basic authorized Nikto scan for one web server. Include scope checks, safe timing, and report format choices.

prompt_templates.title: Tune a Web Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Nikto scan plan for an authorized application. Focus on misconfiguration, information disclosure, and outdated software checks.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare CI Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a CI workflow outline for running Nikto safely, saving reports, and failing only on agreed severity thresholds.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these Nikto findings and produce a prioritized remediation plan with likely false positives, affected assets, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: A security engineer asks for a safe scan plan for one HTTPS server.
output_examples.output: A scoped plan lists authorization checks, the approved target, timing limits, output format, expected traffic impact, and report handling steps.

output_examples.input: A DevOps engineer wants Nikto evidence in a release workflow.
output_examples.output: The response outlines a pipeline stage, artifact retention, severity gates, owner notifications, and manual review before blocking a release.

output_examples.input: A team provides Nikto findings from a web server review.
output_examples.output: The response groups findings by severity, notes likely false positives, maps issues to frameworks, and gives validation and remediation actions.

best_practices: Confirm written authorization, target scope, and scan windows before any test.
Use rate limits, time limits, and approved proxies to reduce operational impact.
Validate Nikto findings manually and document evidence before assigning remediation.
anti_patterns: Scanning systems without explicit written permission.
Running broad scans against production services without rate limits.
Treating Nikto output as final proof without manual verification.

faq.question: Does this skill run Nikto by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples. The user or agent environment must have Nikto installed.

faq.question: Can I scan any public website?
faq.answer: No. Only scan systems you own or have explicit written authorization to test.

faq.question: What report formats does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers text, HTML, CSV, and XML reporting workflows for Nikto scan output.

faq.question: Is this useful for CI/CD?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes pipeline concepts for scan execution, artifacts, and severity gates.

faq.question: Will Nikto find every web vulnerability?
faq.answer: No. Nikto focuses on server issues, known files, misconfigurations, and outdated components.

faq.question: How should I handle false positives?
faq.answer: Verify each finding manually, record evidence, and exclude known false positives from future reports.
